result.title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
result.summary: Foundation models in changing environments can encounter unfamiliar domain knowledge that their original training did not cover. However, new domains rarely provide large amounts of expert-created training data or reliable supervisory signals for further training. We introduce Recursa, a foundation model system that adapts to new domains by learning from its own experience without human experts or a stronger teacher model. Recursa uses a knowledge repository to store what it learns: domain-specific skills and instructions on when to apply them, along with memories of past task experiences and reflections on what to improve. Recursa bootstraps the repository from domain materials and then refines it through recursive self-improvement. It uses parallel learners to execute tasks and synthesize local improvements, then validates and merges the improvements into the knowledge repository. On Harvey LAB's Firm Knowledge benchmark, Recursa raises the all-pass rate on held-out test tasks from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Recursa 系统，让基础模型在缺乏专家数据的新领域中依靠自身经验递归自我改进：用知识库存储领域技能、适用指令、任务记忆与反思，并由并行学习器执行任务、合成局部改进，再经校验合并入库。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉或多模态推理；但其「并行学习器产生多份改进—校验—合并」的流程可为核查多路 latent 状态的生成、验证与归并，以及无强监督下自我生成轨迹的贡献分配提供方法线索。
